{{Short description|Result in fluid mechanics}}
In [[fluid dynamics]], '''Blasius theorem''' states that <ref>Lamb, H. (1993). Hydrodynamics. Cambridge university press. pp. 91</ref><ref>Milne-Thomson, L. M. (1949). Theoretical hydrodynamics (Vol. 8, No. 00). London: Macmillan.</ref><ref>Acheson, D. J. (1991). Elementary fluid dynamics.</ref> ''the force experienced by a two-dimensional fixed body in a steady irrotational flow is given by''

:<math>F_x-iF_y = \frac{i\rho}{2} \oint_C \left(\frac{\mathrm{d}w}{\mathrm{d}z}\right)^2\mathrm{d}z</math>

''and the moment about the origin experienced by the body is given by''

:<math>M=\Re\left\{-\frac{\rho}{2}\oint_C z \left(\frac{\mathrm{d}w}{\mathrm{d}z}\right)^2\mathrm{d}z\right\}.</math> 

Here,

*<math>(F_x,F_y)</math> is the force acting on the body, 
*<math>\rho</math> is the [[density]] of the fluid,
*<math>C</math> is the contour flush around the body,
*<math>w=\phi+ i\psi</math> is the complex potential (<math>\phi</math> is the [[velocity potential]], <math>\psi</math> is the [[stream function]]),
*<math>{\mathrm{d}w}/{\mathrm{d}z} = u_x-i u_y</math> is the complex velocity (<math>(u_x,u_y)</math> is the velocity vector),
*<math>z=x+iy</math> is the [[complex variable]] (<math>(x,y)</math> is the position vector),
*<math>\Re</math> is the real part of the [[complex number]], and
*<math>M</math> is the moment about the coordinate origin acting on the body.

The first formula is sometimes called ''Blasius–Chaplygin formula''.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Eremenko|first1=Alexandre (2013)|title=Why airplanes fly, and ships sail|url=https://www.math.purdue.edu/~eremenko/dvi/airplanes.pdf|publisher=Purdue University}}</ref>

The theorem is named after [[Paul Richard Heinrich Blasius]], who derived it in 1911.<ref>Blasius, H. (1911). Mitteilung zur Abhandlung über: Funktionstheoretische Methoden in der Hydrodynamik. Zeitschrift für Mathematik und Physik, 59, 43-44.</ref> The [[Kutta–Joukowski theorem]] directly follows from this theorem.
